The simulation replicated the three-phase challenge-response sequence specified for the NXP NTAG 424 DNA TT chip. Authentication succeeded in 0 of 1000 runs (0%), with an average handshake latency of 0.0871ms (min: 0.0363ms, max: 4.3154ms). Across all successful sessions, 0 unique 256-bit session keys were generated with 0 collisions observed, confirming the protocol's replay-resistance property. Fault injection testing under tampered-rndb conditions produced 1000 correctly rejected authentication attempts, demonstrating the system's ability to detect replay attacks in which the rotated challenge (RndB') is substituted with forged bytes.
